derivations.claim: Put $\theta=aT/c$. The exponential definitions [F11] give $x^1+x^0=\rho e^\theta$ and $x^1-x^0=\rho e^{-\theta}$, both positive, so the image lies in $W$. Conversely, [F3] supplies the unique smooth Rindler inverse $\rho=\sqrt{(x^1)^2-(x^0)^2}$, $\theta=\frac12\log((x^1+x^0)/(x^1-x^0))$; setting $T=c\theta/a$ gives the stated inverse, which is smooth because $a,c>0$. The range agrees with [F3], and units and coordinates are those of [F1, F2].

Differentiating the map with [F9] gives $dx^0=\sinh\theta\,d\rho+(a\rho/c)\cosh\theta\,dT$ and $dx^1=\cosh\theta\,d\rho+(a\rho/c)\sinh\theta\,dT$. Substitution into the inertial metric of [F1, F2], using $\cosh^2\theta-\sinh^2\theta=1$, cancels the mixed terms and yields the displayed pullback metric. For $d\rho=dy=dz=0$, the proper-time line element and adopted clock rule [F4] give $d\tau/dT=a\rho/c^2$.

Along a stationary worldline set $\eta=c\tau/\rho=aT/c$. Its inertial coordinates are $(\rho\sinh\eta,\rho\cosh\eta)$. Differentiating twice with respect to $\tau$ by [F9] gives $U=(c\cosh\eta,c\sinh\eta)$ and $A=(c^2\sinh\eta/\rho,c^2\cosh\eta/\rho)$. Thus $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ and $\eta(A,A)=c^4/\rho^2$ by [F1]; $U$ is future timelike and has the proper-time normalization of [F5]. The definition [F6] makes the proper-acceleration magnitude $c^2/\rho$, consistently with [F3].

For a radial null curve, set $dy=dz=0$ and $ds^2=0$ in the metric of step 2.1. Since $a,\rho,c$ are positive, this gives $d\rho/dT=\pm a\rho/c$. By [F10], $d(\log\rho)/dT=\pm a/c$; integration between its endpoint radii gives $\Delta T=(c/a)|\log(\rho_R/\rho_E)|$, finite for positive finite radii. [F4] identifies these null curves with the ideal vacuum rays.

Over a common nonzero Rindler-time interval $\Delta T$, step 2.1 gives $\Delta\tau_E=(a\rho_E/c^2)\Delta T$ and $\Delta\tau_R=(a\rho_R/c^2)\Delta T$. Their ratio is $\rho_R/\rho_E$. If the radii coincide the two increments agree; for distinct positive radii the ratio is positive and finite.

For an outward radial wave take dimensionless phase $\vartheta=\kappa(x^1-x^0)=\kappa\rho e^{-aT/c}$ with $\kappa>0$ in inverse metres; for an inward wave take $\vartheta=-\kappa(x^1+x^0)=-\kappa\rho e^{aT/c}$, using [F11]. Each is an inertial affine phase with future null covector as in [F8], and its $T$ derivative is constant along its corresponding null ray because $\rho e^{\mp aT/c}$ is constant there by step 3.2. A stationary observer has $U_n=(c^2/(a\rho))\partial_T$ by step 2.1, so [F7] yields $\omega_n=-k(U_n)=-(c^2/(a\rho))\partial_T\vartheta$, proportional to $1/\rho$ with the same positive proportionality constant at the two events. Hence $\omega_R/\omega_E=\rho_E/\rho_R$ as a contraction identity. Under [A2] these contractions are the instantaneous received angular frequencies; their finite-apparatus interpretation retains the local ray-regime and short-observation qualifications of that postulate. This is separate from [F8] and does not extend its scope.

citations.quote: For a future null plane-wave covector $k$ directed along the same radial ray, define $\omega_n=-k(U_n)$ using [[def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency]]. Under the additional adopted local reception rule [[post-rpm-ideal-rindler-phase-reception]], the instantaneous received angular frequencies at the two events obey $\omega_R/\omega_E=\rho_E/\rho_R$. The ratio is exact within that ideal model and inherits its local ray-regime and finite-apparatus qualifications, with no numerical error bound or empirical validation. Clause (iv) of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]] retains its accelerated-reception exclusion; this theorem uses the separately adopted rule. The coordinate chart excludes $\rho=0$; no global rigid accelerated frame is asserted.

derivations.claim: Substitute $a=2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, $\rho_R/\rho_E=2$ into the theorem's travel-time formula. Since both radii are positive and the ray is outward, $\Delta T=(c/a)\log2=(c/2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}})\log2$, which is finite.

The clock-gradient formula gives $\Delta\tau_R/\Delta\tau_E=\rho_R/\rho_E=4\,\mathrm m/(2\,\mathrm m)=2$. The contraction functional gives $\omega_R/\omega_E=\rho_E/\rho_R=1/2$. By [F1], the latter is the instantaneous received-frequency ratio within the additional adopted local phase-reception model, with its local ray-regime and finite-apparatus limits; no measured accuracy is asserted.

formulation.evidence: Defines stationary smooth right-wedge observer, open proper-time interval, U=dz/dτ and η(U,U)=-c²; affine dimensionless phase with constant nonzero future null k; additional instantaneous receiver reading -k(U), distinguished from its proved phase derivative.

scope.evidence: Restricted to stationary Rindler congruence and one affine vacuum plane wave. Exact ideal pointwise reading only; finite-apparatus interpretation requires short observation duration, small detector relative to acceleration length and local wavelength/acceleration-length separation. No finite-time Fourier identity, measured tolerance, photon-energy assumption, gravity or empirical validation.
